items.stem: Which one of the following was NOT the reason for the popularity of scientific ideas among the common people in eighteenth century Europe ?

options.label: A
options.text: Printing of idea of Isaac Newton

options.label: C
options.text: Interest of people in science and reason

items.answer: Printed editions of Newton's ideas, the spread of the printing press and the general appetite for science and reason all carried scientific thinking to ordinary readers in the eighteenth century. Support from traditional aristocratic groups was not a cause; those groups were in fact the target of much of this new literature. Hence the odd one out is that traditional aristocratic groups supported it.

items.stem: Why was reading of manuscript not easy in India? Choose the appropriate reason from the following options :

options.label: C
options.text: Manuscripts were written in English and Hindi.

items.answer: Indian manuscripts were copied on palm leaf or on hand-made paper, so they were expensive, fragile and easily damaged by handling. They were also written in varied styles and scripts, which made them hard to read. The reason offered here is that manuscripts were fragile.

items.stem: Who were called 'Chapmen?'
items.answer: Chapmen were the petty pedlars who carried cheap printed books from place to place and sold them, so they functioned as book sellers. The printed key marks this as book seller.
items.ocr: Options (a) 'Book seller' and (d) 'Seller of penny chap books' overlap; the printed key chooses (a).

items.stem: Printing was first developed in:
items.answer: The earliest kind of print technology was hand printing, developed in China from about AD 594, where books were rubbed off from woodblocks onto paper. Printing therefore first developed in China.

items.stem: When was leading libraries came into existence?
items.answer: The printed solution rejects all three dated choices and settles on 'None of above'.
items.ocr: Printed key reads '(b) None of above', but option (b) is 'Seventeenth century' and 'None of above' is option (d). The solution text wins, so the key is recorded as D.

items.stem: Who was Martin Luther?
items.answer: Martin Luther was the sixteenth century religious reformer whose Ninety Five Theses attacked the practices of the Roman Catholic Church and began the Protestant Reformation. He was a religious reformer.
items.concept: Religious debate and the fear of print

items.stem: Identify the picture-
items.answer: The photograph shows the long wooden halls of the depository at Haein Temple in Korea, where the woodblocks of the Buddhist canon are stored in row upon row of shelves. This is the Tripitaka Koreana.

items.stem:
Arrange the following options in the correct sequence-
1. Press came to be made out of metal.
2. Offset press was developed.
3. Gutenberg perfected the system by olive press.
4. China first introduced hand- printing technology into Japan.
items.answer: Hand printing passed from China to Japan first; Gutenberg then perfected the press using the olive press design in the fifteenth century; by the mid-nineteenth century presses were being built out of metal; the offset press, which could print in several colours, came last. The order is 4, 3, 2, 1.
items.ocr: The printed sequence '4, 3, 2, 1' places the metal press before the offset press, although the list numbers them 1 and 2 respectively.

items.stem: Which scholar expressed a deep anxiety about printing?
items.answer: Erasmus, the Latin scholar and Catholic reformer, wrote that printed books would flood the world with matter that was irreligious and rebellious, and so voiced a deep anxiety about print. The answer is Erasmus.
items.concept: Religious debate and the fear of print

items.stem: Which of the following cities became the hub of the Western style-school culture printing?
items.answer: As Western-style schools spread in China, Shanghai became the centre of the new print culture serving them. The city is Shanghai.

items.stem: In which of the following years, Buddhist missionaries from China introduced hand-printing technology?
items.answer: Buddhist missionaries from China introduced hand-printing technology into Japan around AD 768-770. The correct span is 768-770 AD.

items.stem: Assertion : The first book that Gutenberg printed was the Bible. Reason : About 500 copies were printed and it took two years to produce them.
items.assertion: The first book that Gutenberg printed was the Bible.
items.reason: About 500 copies were printed and it took two years to produce them.

items.answer: Gutenberg's first printed book was indeed the Bible, so the assertion is true. But about 180 copies were printed, not 500, so the reason is false. Assertion is true but reason is false.

items.stem: Which of the following authors from New York had perfected the power-driven cylindrical press?
items.answer: By the mid-nineteenth century Richard M. Hoe of New York had perfected the power-driven cylindrical press, capable of 8,000 sheets an hour. The answer is Richard M. Hoe.

items.stem:
Arrange the following books in the ascending order of the dates of their publication-
1. 'Kesari' written by Balgangadhar Tilak.
2. 'Gulamgiri' written by Jyotiba Phule.
3. 1ˢᵗ printed edition of 'The Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas'.
4. 'The Sambad Kaumudi' published by Ram Mohan Roy.
items.answer: The first printed edition of the Ramcharitmanas came out in 1810, the Sambad Kaumudi was started in 1821, Gulamgiri was published in 1871 and Kesari began in 1881. In ascending order of date this gives 3, 4, 2, 1.

items.stem: At which of the following places in India, first printing press was established?
items.answer: The printing press came to India with Portuguese missionaries, who set up the first press at Goa in the mid-sixteenth century. The place is Goa.

items.stem:

• Was the son of a merchant
• perfected the system by olive press in 1448
items.answer: A German goldsmith, the son of a merchant, who adapted the olive press and built the first known printing press by 1448 can only be Johann Gutenberg.

items.stem: Assertion : The production of handwritten manuscripts could not satisfy the ever-increasing demand for books. Reason : Chinese paper reached Europe via the silk route.
items.assertion: The production of handwritten manuscripts could not satisfy the ever-increasing demand for books.
items.reason: Chinese paper reached Europe via the silk route.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Copying by hand was slow, costly and laborious, so manuscripts could never meet the rising demand for books; that much is true. It is also true that Chinese paper came to Europe along the silk route, but the supply of paper is not the explanation for the shortfall of handwritten books. Both are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation.
items.ocr: The question number is partly hidden by the NODIA watermark; read as 20 from the surrounding sequence.

items.stem: Which of the following countries had the earliest kind of print technology?
items.answer: The earliest kind of print technology, hand printing from woodblocks, was developed in China, Japan and Korea. All three are therefore correct.

items.stem: What is calligraphy?
items.answer: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful and stylised writing, used in manuscripts before the coming of print. The answer is stylised writing.

items.stem: Which one of the following option best signifies this picture?

options.label: B
options.text: Cultural impact of the west which has turned the family upside down.

options.label: D
options.text: Teaching women how to be obedient wires.

items.answer: The print shows a wife, dressed in Western fashion, holding her husband by a chain while he kneels before her - a conservative cartoon mocking the reversal of household order. The printed key reads it as the destruction of proper family relations.
items.ocr: Option (d) printed as 'obedient wires' (for 'wives'). Options (b) and (c) are close in sense; the printed key chooses (c).

items.stem: Which of the following classes emerged as a new reading class?
items.answer: The printed key identifies the elite class as the new reading class.

items.stem:
Arrange the following countries on the basis of "Print technology" started in these countries-
1. Japan
2. China
3. Korea
4. India
items.answer: Hand printing began in China, passed to Japan with Buddhist missionaries, was used in Korea, and reached India only with the Portuguese in the sixteenth century. The printed order is 2, 1, 3, 4.

items.stem: At which place, Catholic priests printed the first Tamil book in 1579?
items.answer: Catholic priests printed the first Tamil book at Cochin in 1579. The place is Cochin.

items.stem: Assertion : The new reading culture was accompanied by a new technology. Reason : From hand printing there was a gradual shift to mechanical printing.

items.answer: The spread of reading rested on the shift from slow hand printing to mechanical presses, which made books cheap and plentiful. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

items.stem: Which of the following countries possessed a huge bureaucratic system which recruited its personnel through Civil Service Examination?
items.answer: Imperial China ran a vast bureaucracy recruited through civil service examinations, and the state printed the textbooks for these examinations in huge numbers. The country is China.

items.stem: Which of the following books is the oldest Japanese book, printed in AD containing six sheets of text and woodcut illustrations?
items.answer: The oldest Japanese book, printed in AD 868, is the Buddhist Diamond Sutra, made of six sheets of text and woodcut illustrations. The answer is Diamond Sutra.

items.stem: Who introduced the printing press in India?
items.answer: Portuguese missionaries brought the printing press to Goa in the mid-sixteenth century. The Portuguese introduced it.

items.stem: Assertion : Print and popular religious literature stimulated many distinctive individual interpretations of faith even among little-educated working people. Reason : Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, literacy rates went up in most parts of Europe.

items.answer: Cheap religious print did let even barely schooled people read and interpret faith for themselves, as Menocchio's case shows, so the assertion is true. Rising literacy in seventeenth and eighteenth century Europe is also true, but it is not what explains those individual readings of faith. Both true, reason not the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which book of Jyotiba Phule was based on the caste system?
items.answer: Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgiri in 1871, an attack on the injustices of the caste system. The book is Gulamgiri.

items.stem: At which of the following places, the Grimm Brothers spent years compiling traditional folk tales gathered from peasants?
items.answer: The Grimm Brothers in Germany spent years gathering and editing traditional folk tales collected from peasants. The place is Germany.

items.stem: Which of the following is/are some of the best-known women novelist during 19th century?
items.answer: Jane Austen, George Eliot and the Bronte sisters were all celebrated women novelists of the nineteenth century, and their writing defined a new image of woman as a person with will and intelligence. All of these is correct.

items.stem: What did Menocchio, the miller, do?
items.answer: Menocchio, a miller in sixteenth century Italy, read the books he could get hold of and reinterpreted the message of the Bible, formulating a view of God and Creation that enraged the Roman Catholic Church, which finally executed him.

items.answer: Before print reached them, the common people lived in a world of oral culture, hearing sacred texts read out, ballads recited and folk tales narrated. The answer is common people.

items.answer: The printed key names the European countries.

items.stem: Which one of the following, created the possibility of wide circulation of ideas, and introduced a new world of debate and discussion?
items.answer: Print made ideas cheap and plentiful, so they could circulate widely and be argued over publicly. Print created that new world of debate and discussion.
items.concept: Religious debate and the fear of print

items.stem: Who wrote My Childhood and My University?
items.answer: The Russian writer Maxim Gorky wrote the autobiographical books My Childhood and My University, which were read widely by workers. The author is Maxim Gorky.

items.stem: Who was James Lackington?
items.answer: James Lackington was a London bookseller and publisher of the late eighteenth century, remembered for selling cheap books in great numbers. He was a publisher.

items.stem: What was Gutenberg's first printed book?
items.answer: The first book Gutenberg printed on his new press was the Bible, completed by 1455. The answer is the Bible.

items.stem: In which of the two languages, 50 books were published in 1674?
items.answer: By 1674 about 50 books had been printed in the Konkani and Kanara languages by the Catholic missionaries in the west of India. The languages are Konkani and Kanada.

items.stem: What were Penny Chapbooks?
items.answer: Penny chapbooks were cheap pocket-sized books, carried by pedlars and sold for a penny so that even the poor could buy them. They were pocket-sized books.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in the correct sequence of old tradition of handwritten manuscripts:
1. Vernacular languages
2. Persian
3. Arabic
4. Sanskrit
items.answer: India's old tradition of handwritten manuscripts runs from Sanskrit, through Arabic and Persian, to the various vernacular languages. The order is 4, 3, 2, 1.

items.answer: Martin Luther wrote the Ninety Five Theses in 1517, attacking the practices and rituals of the Roman Catholic Church. The reformer is Martin Luther.

items.answer: From 1780 James Augustus Hickey edited the Bengal Gazette, a weekly magazine that carried commercial news and gossip about the Company's officials. The editor is James Augustus Hickey.

items.stem: Who began to publish the weekly Bengal Gazette?
items.answer: Gangadhar Bhattacharya, close to Rammohun Roy, began publishing the weekly Bengal Gazette, one of the first Indian-run papers. The answer is Gangadhar Bhattacharya.

items.stem: At which of the following places, a children's press was set up in 1857?
items.answer: A children's press devoted entirely to books for children was set up in France in 1857. The place is France.
